messages:
alex: Quick sync — RFC follow-up about the adaptive-priority ingest queue we discussed yesterday. I pushed a strawman policy in the doc (link: https://go/redwood/obs-priority-rfc) and want to capture concerns before we lock the contract. TL;DR: front proxy assigns a priority score (0-100), we translate to a budget token rate per tenant, and the ingest gateway enforces per-tenant token consumption with soft and hard limits.

maria: skimmed the doc. two immediate questions: 1) where does priority come from? customer header vs inferred? 2) how deterministic is sampling under overload? we need reproducibility for billing.

alex: good Qs. proposal: priority provenance order = (explicit header) > (route override for internal routes) > (edge heuristic). header must include a signed provenance tag when coming from trusted gateway. if missing, gateway emits an inferred priority with origin=proxy.

alex: determinism: during overload we use a deterministic hash-based token bucket for sampling so the same request shape + tenant gets consistent decision for some time window. not perfect, but reproducible for post-hoc audits.

 tj: quick nit — hash windows need care. if we use a low-cardinality key (trace id prefix) we might bias hot users. prefer combining tenant_id + priority_score + epoch.

 alex: agreed. plan: sampling_key = sha256(tenant_id + priority_score + coarse_epoch) % 10000. coarse_epoch = floor(now / 60) by default.

 sylvia: what about enrichment + late-binding billing keys? lots of traces are missing tenant attribution until enrichment. if we drop early, we'll lose everything for that trace.

 maria: this is the big tradeoff. dropping pre-enrichment reduces cost but biases against traces that only become billable after late enrichment. we should support a small "quarantine buffer" where spans with unresolved billing are retained for a short grace period (e.g., 5s) and re-evaluated after late enrichment resolves billing_key.

 alex: yes — quarantine buffer is in the strawman: small in-memory queue per ingress worker (configurable size, default 2000 events). events older than buffer_age are subject to lower priority sampling. we also emit a metric: quarantine_fill_pct and quarantine_drop_count.

 tj: operations question: this design moves memory pressure into ingress workers. during cluster-wide overload that could OOM many processes. can we implement a shared eviction ring instead of per-worker queue?

 sylvia: shared ring reduces per-process OOM risk but adds contention and complexity for exactly-once semantics. maybe start with per-worker soft limits + a global backpressure signal to reduce emit rate upstream (edge proxy).

 alex: agreed. step 1: per-worker quarantine + global backpressure counter (ingest-broker sets X-off when aggregated quarantine usage > threshold). step 2 (future): experiment with shared in-memory ring using sharded memstore.

 maria: metrics / SLOs we need to track: per-tenant drop_rate, quarantine_hit_rate, post-enrich_recovery_rate (how many recovered after enrichment), cost_per_minute, and latency p99 for ingest path. also alert when priority_signals_from_edge drop unexpectedly.

 tj: API contract suggestion: the gateway -> ingest envelope should include these headers (example):

```json
{"x-rd-priority": "73", "x-rd-priority-origin": "edge-proxy", "x-rd-priority-sig": "v1:base64sig", "x-rd-emit-ts": "1680000000"}
```

 tia: (typo) I meant tj above. also: need TTL on the signature to avoid replay. we should validate signature but allow unsigned when origin=internal-dev.

 alex: we already added expiry in the proto. signature contains expiry epoch, tenant_id, and nonce. validators drop signatures outside allowed clock skew (configurable).

 sylvia: how do we expose sampling decisions to customers for explainability? e.g., "why was trace X dropped?" we should persist decision metadata as a sparse event stored with minimal footprint.

 alex: idea: emit a compact sampling-decision event into a cold topic (kafka) that contains {trace_stub, tenant_id, decision, reason, sample_seed, enqueue_ts}. consumers can join this with retained envelopes for debug. size is small and retained for 7 days by default.

 maria: we must be careful with PII on those decision events — scrub any payload and only include opaque ids. already in doc but calling it out.

 tj: cost allocation stuff — if we drop pre-enrichment and later enrichment would have attributed to a high-value tenant, finance will complain. We need a reconciliation signal: estimate lost revenue by sampling a small deterministic fraction of quarantined-drops and keep them to feed billing model.

 alex: proposal: keep a deterministic 0.1% mirror sample of dropped pre-enriched events (seeded by tenant + epoch). send to dedicated pipeline labeled as "recon_sample". finance can run periodic recon on that to estimate leakage.

 sylvia: we also need a feature flag to allow some tenants to opt out of dropping (SLO-backed tenants). config shape: 

```yaml
priority_overrides:
  tenant-123:
    min_tokens_per_minute: 1000
    hold_quarantine: true
```

 alex: yes — this ties into Dedicated offering. default plan: shared tenancy has normal policy, dedicated tenants can set preservation knobs.

 ingest-bot: deploy-note: added preliminary config flags "quarantine_size", "coarse_epoch_secs", "deterministic_mirror_pct" to staging config. rolled to staging/ingest-01 at 3577770300.

 maria: testing plan: 1) unit tests for hash-seed determinism 2) chaos test with controlled overload to verify global backpressure triggers 3) e2e with late-enrichment pipeline to ensure post-enrich recovery works within buffer window.

 tj: one more ops thing — hot-tenant protection. if a single tenant floods priority=100, we need to cap absolute tokens per-tenant and bleed into a fairness pool. otherwise noisy neighbor problem.

 alex: fairness design: two-level budgeting: tenant_budget = min(configured_max, token_rate_by_priority); fairness_pool drains excess when overall utilization < threshold; when saturated, tenant budgets clipped proportionally. We'll add telemetry: tenant_clamp_count and fairness_clipped_pct.

 sylvia: sounds good. next steps: alex/ops to refine the contract and add sequence diagrams for edge->ingest->enrichment flow, Maria to draft alert runbook, TJ to prototype the deterministic mirror sampler. I'll merge the doc after we get these items.

 alex: thanks — I'll update the RFC with quarantine details and the sample event schema. ping me in DMs if you want to pair on proto changes. :+1:
